picks.title: Airy functions from quantum M-theory
picks.abstract: We show that Airy function partition functions for M2-brane theories may be derived from relative equivariant localization of quantum M-theory. The eleven-dimensional Chern–Simons coupling gives the cubic term in the grand potential, while the X 8 correction gives the charge shift. Fixing the M2-brane charge turns the localized M-theory path integral into an Airy integral. In this way we derive the ABJM result, its toric Calabi–Yau generalizations, and gravitational blocks for black holes and other spacetimes, up to the prefactor and non-perturbative corrections.

picks.title: The Explosion Time of the Jittering Jet Explosion Mechanism (JJEM)
picks.abstract: We compare the expected explosion time of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) to that in the neutrino-driven (the delayed neutrino) mechanism, and conclude that for most, but not all, stellar models, even when the neutrino-driven mechanism might have led to an explosion, the JJEM starts to operate before the neutrino mechanism fully revives the stalled shock. To achieve this goal, we conduct comprehensive one-dimensional stellar evolution simulations using the code mesa to determine the expected explosion time according to the JJEM, which corresponds to the time when the inner convective layer of the core is accreted onto the newly born neutron star (NS). We present results for many hydrogen-rich, hydrogen-stripped, and helium+hydrogen-stripped envelope CCSN progenitor models. We find that most, but not all, of our models in the initial mass range of M ZAMS = 12 M ⊙ to M ZAMS = 40 M ⊙ , have at least one strong convective zone inside the mass coordinate that is the maximum baryonic mass of an NS, m ≃ 2.65 M ⊙ , which can facilitate the JJEM. This study contributes to establishing the JJEM as a viable explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

picks.title: Lattice QCD determination of the γ Z box contribution to the proton weak charge
picks.abstract: We present the first lattice QCD determination of the γ Z box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, ▫ γ Z , a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to E = 155 MeV. At E = 0 , the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain ▫ γ Z ( 0 ) = 0.00411 ( 9 ) . Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of Q W p = 0.06987 ( 50 ) . The calculated energy dependence of ▫ γ Z is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract Q W p . Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the γ Z box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.

picks.title: A New Bayesian Framework with Mass–Radius–Space Priors to Constrain the Neutron Star Equation of State
picks.abstract: We propose a new Bayesian framework to infer the neutron star equation of state (EOS) from mass and radius observations and neutron matter theory by defining priors that directly parameterize mass–radius space instead of pressure–energy density space. We use direct and accurate inversion approximations to map mass–radius relations to the underlying EOS. We systematically compare its EOS inferences with those inferred from traditional EOS parameterizations, taking care to quantify the systematic prior uncertainties of both. Our results show that prior uncertainties should be included in all Bayesian approaches. The alternative framework provides broader and more uniform coverage of the physically allowed mass–radius space, especially small radius configurations, with enhanced computational efficiency. Substantially reduced dependence on prior choices seems to result from having both prior and posterior distributions in the same observational mass–radius space. Results indicate that direct parameterization in observed space offers a robust and efficient alternative to traditional methods.

picks.title: Discerning between Excimer and Singlet Fission Sites Using Modulated Magnetic Field Photoluminescence
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Magnetic field effects play a key role in the characterization of organic electronic materials. In particular, the microscopic processes underlying singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation have been clarified in recent years through the observation and subsequent theoretical explanation of magnetic field effects in these processes. Here, we study magnetic field effects on the luminescence of 5,12-bis((triisopropylsilyl)ethynyl)tetracene, a well-studied material in which both singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation occur. By performing highly sensitive modulated-field magneto-photoluminescence experiments we observe magnetic field effect lineshapes with rich detail, allowing a precise characterization of triplet exciton dynamics. By additionally filtering these magnetic field effects by luminescence wavelength, we can identify the excimer state by its unique magnetic field signature. Finally, we show that a theoretical explanation of these field effects requires a model that explicitly accounts for quantum coherences, which highlights the importance of detailed spin dynamics modeling in understanding magnetic field effects, even at room temperature.

picks.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
picks.abstract: Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense 5 .

picks.title: Enhancing Grignard Reactions via Anion Borrowing in Deep Eutectic/Organic Biphasic Media
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as powerful reaction media to enhance nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules. In this protocol, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i-PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results demonstrate enhanced chemoselectivity for the Grignard addition over β-H transfer side reaction from the isopropyl group when in DES/THF. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the neutral Grignard species in neat THF kinetically favors β-H transfer, chloride enrichment from the DES renders both pathways kinetically competitive and markedly increases the thermodynamic preference for the addition product through enhanced intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these nonconventional solvents.

Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis
picks.abstract: Endometriosis is a painful and heterogeneous condition that affects up to one in ten women. Its genetic underpinnings remain partially unknown, and its precise disease mechanisms are yet to be elucidated. Here we report a genome-wide study of endometriosis as part of the Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative representing over 1 million participants (32% non-European ancestry). We detected 58 genomic regions (27 previously unreported) across diverse ancestry groups and new procedure-confirmed case identification algorithms. These include loci unique to African and admixed American populations. A search for genetically driven comorbidities revealed dozens of associations with known and previously uncharacterized risk factors. Then, within prioritized cellular contexts, we found numerous examples of gene expression affected by endometriosis status. Including further multiomic analyses, we implicated a total of 314 genes, suggesting multiple targets for therapeutic intervention. Our findings span molecular, cellular and phenotypic scales, highlighting interconnected pathways that underscore the multifaceted etiology of endometriosis.

picks.title: Collusion through Common Leadership
picks.abstract: This paper studies whether common leadership, defined as two firms sharing executives or board directors, contributes to collusion. Using an explicit measure of labor market collusion from unsealed court evidence, we find that the probability of collusion between two firms increases by 11 percentage points after the onset of common leadership, a ninefold increase over the baseline rate. These results are not driven by closeness of product or labor market competition. Our findings are consistent with the increasing attention toward common leadership under Clayton Act Section 8. more.title: Muon Lifetime and Fermi Constant: An Update
more.abstract: We present an updated prediction for the lifetime of the muon, including a detailed analysis of all relevant uncertainties. Our prediction includes QED corrections up to order α 3 and state-of-the-art hadronic contributions based on dispersive methods. Radiative corrections and finite-electron-mass effects are parametrized by the correction factor Δ q in τ μ − 1 = G F 2 m μ 5 ( 1 + Δ q ) / ( 192 π 3 ) , for which we obtain Δ q = ( − 4 384 700 ± 34 ) × 10 − 9 . This reduces the uncertainty associated with Δ q by an order of magnitude compared to the previous prediction at order α 2 . We use our results to provide an updated value of the Fermi coupling constant, G F = 1.166 378 60 ( 59 ) × 10 − 5 GeV − 2 (consistent with the current Particle Data Group estimate). Further improvements will require better measurements of the muon lifetime and mass.

more.title: MAGNUS. III. Mild Evolution of the Total Density Slope in Massive Early-type Galaxies Since z ∼ 1 from Dynamical Modeling of MUSE Integral-field Stellar Kinematics
more.abstract: We investigate the total mass density slope evolution in massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) over the last 6.5 Gyr (0 < z < 0.75). We perform a detailed dynamical analysis of approximately 200 ETGs spanning the redshift range of 0.24 < z < 0.75, utilizing spatially resolved stellar kinematics derived from high signal-to-noise ratio MUSE-DEEP spectroscopy and surface brightness models from high-resolution Hubble Space Telescope imaging. We constrain mass distributions using the Jeans anisotropic modeling technique coupled with the multi-Gaussian expansion method. To rigorously constrain evolutionary trends, we combine this intermediate-redshift data set with a local ETG sample ( z ∼ 0.05) from the MaNGA survey. We adopt dynamical constraints for the local sample derived using an identical homogeneous methodology, ensuring a strictly consistent comparison. We found that the total density profiles of the intermediate-redshift ETG sample are approximately isothermal and exhibit a median mass-weighted total density slope, γ T = 2.19 ± 0.01 at z = 0.44 , which is shallower than the local baseline of γ T = 2.26 ± 0.01 at z = 0.04 . This structural shift corresponds to a redshift gradient of d γ T / d z ≈ −0.20 ± 0.03, detected at ∼6 σ significance. We demonstrate that this trend is robust against model assumptions and persists even when restricting the analysis to high-velocity dispersion systems ( σ e > 150 km s −1 ). Our findings are consistent with previous lensing-based studies and in tension with cosmological simulations. The observed steepening suggests that dissipative processes, such as gas-rich accretion and mergers, must play a nonnegligible role in the late-stage assembly of massive ETGs.

more.title: High-temperature η -pairing superconductivity in the photodoped Hubbard model
more.abstract: We investigate superconductivity emerging in the photodoped Mott insulating Hubbard model using steady-state dynamical mean-field theory implemented on the real-frequency axis. By employing high-order strong-coupling impurity solvers, we obtain the nonequilibrium phase diagram for photoinduced η -pairing superconductivity with a remarkably high effective critical temperature. We further identify a superconducting gap in the momentum-resolved spectral function and optical conductivity, providing spectroscopic signatures accessible to experiments. Our results highlight a route to a controllable form of high-temperature superconductivity in nonequilibrium strongly correlated systems, fundamentally distinct from the equilibrium s -wave pairing state in the attractive Hubbard model or cuprate-like d -wave superconductors.

more.title: Reaching for the Edge. II. Stellar Halos out to Large Radii as a Tracer of Dark Matter Halo Mass
more.abstract: The diffuse outskirts of brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) encode valuable information about the assembly history and mass of their host dark matter halos. However, the low surface brightness of these stellar halos has historically made them difficult to observe. Recent deep imaging, particularly with Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC), has shown that the stellar mass within large projected annuli, such as 50 and 100 kpc, is a promising proxy for halo mass. However, the optimal radial definition of this “outskirt mass” remains uncertain. We construct an HSC-like mock observing pipeline to measure stellar mass density profiles of BCGs in the IllustrisTNG simulations. The resulting profiles reproduce HSC profiles across 6 orders of magnitude in surface density. We then measure stellar masses within different annuli and how tightly they connect to halo mass. Stellar masses measured within simple apertures exhibit more scatter in the stellar mass–halo mass relation than those measured within projected ellipsoidal annuli. We identify an optimal range, with inner radii of ∼60–300 kpc and outer radii of ∼250–500 kpc. We also introduce two halo-mass-dependent Sérsic models for average stellar halo profiles. The first depends only on halo mass, M vir , and has a median error of 0.19 dex (∼54%). Adding the central stellar mass of the BCG as a second parameter reduces this to 0.15 dex (∼39%). Together, these results provide fitting functions for BCG stellar halos that can be applied to future wide-field surveys to infer halo masses from deep imaging data.

more.title: Generic long-range correlations in conserved nonequilibrium mixtures
more.abstract: We study correlation functions in conserved nonequilibrium mixtures, including multi-temperature systems and non-reciprocal field theories. The corresponding linear theory is short-ranged, and nonlinearities are irrelevant in the renormalization-group sense. Nonetheless, we find that these nonlinearities generate long-ranged three-point correlations in the isotropic disordered phase. Our analytical predictions, which are based on a phenomenological theory, are confirmed by numerical simulations of Brownian colloids in contact with thermal baths at different temperatures. Dangerously irrelevant nonlinearities in nonequilibrium mixtures thus offer a new route to long-range correlations, supporting the hypothesis that such correlations are not the exception but the rule out of equilibrium.

more.title: Fundamental limits of large momentum transfer in optical lattices
more.abstract: Large-momentum-transfer techniques are instrumental for the next generation of atom interferometers as they significantly improve their sensitivity. State-of-the-art implementations rely on elastic scattering processes from optical lattices such as Bloch oscillations or sequential Bragg diffraction, but their performance is constrained by imperfect pulse efficiencies. Here we develop a Floquet-based theoretical framework that provides a unified description of elastic light–atom scattering across all relevant regimes. This formalism enables an efficient exploration of the parameter space, including quasi-momentum preparation, and reveals previously unexplored operating regimes in which tailored Floquet states exhibit orders-of-magnitude reduced losses. In addition, phase extrema of excited Floquet states provide enhanced robustness against lattice-parameter fluctuations. The model is validated through direct comparison with numerical solutions of the Schrödinger equation and through quantitative agreement with recent experimental benchmark results. Our findings establish new, practical operating regimes for large-momentum-transfer beam splitters and open promising perspectives for precision atom interferometry in fundamental physics, gravity gradiometry, and gravitational-wave detection.

more.title: Evolving Dark Energy Is Vacuum Energy After All
more.abstract: We investigate a physically motivated model of dynamical dark energy (DE) arising from the nonperturbative topological structure of the quantum chromodynamics (QCD) vacuum. The model introduces no new fundamental field or propagating degree of freedom: the DE density emerges as a global vacuum response to an expanding spacetime. We develop the first comprehensive cosmological implementation of this QCD-DE scenario and confront it with current observations, including Planck, the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, and South Pole Telescope (SPT-3G) cosmic microwave background data, Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, and Type Ia supernova samples from Pantheon+ and DES-Dovekie. We compare the model with ΛCDM and w 0 w a CDM cosmologies. The model provides an excellent fit to the data and reproduces the late-time DE evolution preferred by DESI. The model naturally predicts effective phantom crossing behaviour at intermediate redshifts ( z ∼ 0.67) while avoiding the instabilities associated with phantom scalar fields. Using goodness-of-fit statistics and Bayesian model-selection tools, including Akaike and deviance information criteria and Bayesian evidence estimated from Markov Chain Monte Carlo chains, we find that the QCD-induced model is consistently favored over ΛCDM for the full combination of early- and late-time datasets. Unlike the conventional descriptions of dynamical DE, support for QCD-DE in Bayesian evidence remains more consistent across datasets, suggesting that a physically motivated departure from a cosmological constant may provide a more economical description of the expansion history preferred by current observations.

more.title: On the Origin of Anomalous Dissipation in Simulations of Tidal Disruption Events
more.abstract: In a tidal disruption event (TDE), a star is destroyed by the tidal field of a supermassive black hole. The stellar debris is initially placed on highly elliptical orbits, and a longstanding question in TDE theory is: how does the stellar debris circularize into a disk and accrete? The originally proposed answer to this question is self-intersection shocks, where relativistic apsidal precession results in a strong collision between the incoming and outgoing material. However, global simulations of TDEs tend to find enhanced hydrodynamical dissipation prior to any intersections of the debris orbits, with the material “fanning out” into a wide-angle and partially unbound outflow upon passing through pericenter. We show that this dissipation is numerical in origin and arises from a combination of (1) the change in the kinematics of the debris as it passes through pericenter, with its velocity profile along the stream transitioning from strongly diverging pre-pericenter to strongly converging post-pericenter, and (2) the dependence of numerical algorithms (viscosity switches for particle-based methods and Riemann solvers for Godunov-based schemes) on the diverging versus converging nature of the fluid. We support this conclusion with analytical and numerical modeling. We discuss possible resolutions to these issues as well as the implications of our findings in the context of observations.

more.title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
more.abstract: One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics…

Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
more.abstract: . These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with AD and age-matched non-dementia control participants. We show that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, showing notable changes in both volumes and gene expression during ageing and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. These signatures were reflected in specific cell types: microglia transitioned to a pro-inflammatory state, whereas inhibitory neurons within sleep-regulating and circadian-regulating hypothalamic subregions showed the most profound transcriptional alterations, including disruptions in ligand-receptor interactions and G-protein-coupled receptor signalling. HypoAD provides a high-resolution volumetric map and a transcriptomic atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, relating lifestyle and behavioural changes to the relevant volumetric and molecular pathways. In addition, HypoAD provides a framework to investigate hypothalamic dysfunction and establishes a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating physiological disruptions to potentially slow disease progression.

more.title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
more.abstract: , the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria, guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei. Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial-chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

more.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
more.abstract: Wernicke's area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke's area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke's area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

more.title: 1,8-Azulenedicarboxylic Imides: Excited-State Properties and Catalytic Activity of a Nonalternant π-System
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Imide-functionalized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) represent an important class of π-conjugated molecules; however, their nonalternant isomers remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis and investigation of the structural, photophysical, and excited-state properties of 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides as nonalternant isomers of 1,8-naphthalimides. These compounds retain the characteristic photophysics of the azulene framework, including near-infrared (NIR) absorption and anti-Kasha emission, while substitution at the imide nitrogen enables modulation of their excited-state electronic structures. QD-NEVPT2 calculations identified an S2–T1 pair with relatively large SOC and LE-to-CT character, suggesting a plausible ISC pathway associated with the observed singlet-oxygen photosensitization. Consequently, 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides function as an effective visible-light photocatalyst for the α-cyanation of secondary and tertiary amines. These findings demonstrate that the present nonalternant molecular design provides a strategy for tuning excited-state properties by modulating locally excited and charge-transfer states in imide chromophores.

more.title: Composition-Driven Discovery of Multimetallic Catalysts Using Features Inspired by the Virtual Crystal Approximation
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Structure–activity relationships built on structure-derived descriptors are a dominant paradigm in catalyst screening. However, this structure-driven framework scales poorly to multimetallic systems, where active sites are heterogeneous, dynamically reconstruct under operating conditions, and require extensive structural enumeration and system-specific descriptor engineering. Here, we introduce a composition-driven screening strategy for multimetallic catalysts using feature construction inspired by the virtual crystal approximation. Specifically, multimetallic sites are represented as composition-weighted pseudoatoms, allowing readily available elemental properties to be converted into predictive features without explicit structural modeling. Unlike elemental fractions alone, these features encode physicochemical differences among the constituent metals. We demonstrate this approach using Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) as a compositionally tunable and reconstruction-prone validation platform for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Combining the composition-derived features with symbolic regression yields an explicit expression for ranking compositions, guiding experimental identification of four high-performance PBAs. We further evaluate this strategy across six literature data sets spanning different catalyst families and reactions, independently training a model for each. Using one of the models, we screen and experimentally validate a perovskite catalyst achieving an overpotential of 189 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in acidic OER. These results demonstrate the broad applicability of virtual crystal approximation-inspired feature construction for composition-driven screening of multimetallic catalysts.

more.title: High-Throughput Screening of Photocatalytic Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Reduction Using Relational Data Extraction and Hierarchical Machine Learning
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Photocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction (CO2RR) over metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is governed by both framework features and reaction conditions, which complicate catalyst discovery and render general design rules difficult to establish. In this study, we develop a synergistic machine-learning workflow to integrate literature data extraction, electronic-property prediction, and hierarchical classification for prioritizing MOF photocatalysts. First, a literature-derived record-level data set containing catalyst compositions, structural descriptors, reaction conditions, and catalytic outcomes was curated through large language model (LLM)-assisted relation extraction followed by manual verification. Then, a transfer-learning crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) model was trained for band gap prediction at the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional (HSE06) level, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 eV against reference HSE06 calculations. Subsequently, a physically constrained multitask framework was employed to predict electron affinity (EA) and ionization potential (IP) for thermodynamic prescreening. Three record-level classifiers were constructed for activity screening (C1), performance classification (C2), and product selectivity prediction (C3). When applied to the Computation-Ready, Experimental (CoRE) MOF database under standardized gas- and liquid-phase inference settings, the workflow prioritized 639 primary candidates, with most assigned to CO formation. Probability calibration and applicability-domain analysis further identified 166 of these candidates (25.98%) as a more stringent calibrated, in-domain subset. Overall, this study provides a practical data-driven workflow for condition-resolved prioritization of MOF…

more.title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
more.abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

more.title: Phototunable Solid–Liquid Interfacial Energy via Ion–Electron Coupling
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: The solid–liquid interfacial energy governs wetting, adhesion, and friction, yet is commonly regarded as a static property defined by surface chemistry and liquid composition. Here we show that light can reversibly modulate the interfacial energy at chemically invariant semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces by tuning the electrostatic coupling between electronic carriers in the solid and ions in the liquid. Using dark dynamic tensiometry, we directly quantify photoinduced changes in advancing and receding contact angles, revealing pronounced and reversible wettability modulation that is absent on insulating or metallic substrates. Systematic control experiments indicate that, in simple salt electrolytes, the response arises primarily from electrostatic coupling between photomodulated carriers and mobile ions in the electric double layer, rather than from detectable photochemical surface modification or changes in bulk liquid properties. In situ atomic force microscopy and ionovoltaic measurements provide microscopic and quantitative evidence that light attenuates or enhances electrostatic double-layer forces and ion–electron coupling, and reveal a sign reversal in the photoresponse between PFOTS-modified and bare Si interfaces. The opposing responses of PFOTS-modified and bare interfaces persist on p-type Si, showing that the effect is not confined to n-type substrates. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this phototunable coupling extends to reversible control of kinetic friction, enabling active modulation of droplet sliding dynamics. These results also identify imaging light as a potential source of bias in contact-angle measurements at photoactive semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces. These findings establish ion–electron coupling as a tunable thermodynamic lever…

more.title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation
more.abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron-containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

more.title: Superconducting Half-Dome in Bilayer Nickelates
more.abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges and collapses in correlated electron systems remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics. As a recently discovered member of the high temperature superconductor family, bilayer nickelates provide a new opportunity for examining this problem. Their pronounced sensitivity to oxygen stoichiometry, while posing challenges for stabilizing superconductivity, simultaneously offers an effective control parameter for tuning electronic phases. Here we report a superconducting half-dome in compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films as a function of continuous tuning of oxygen stoichiometry. Starting from an optimally superconducting state, increasing oxygen stoichiometry gradually suppresses superconductivity toward a metallic phase, whereas decreasing oxygen stoichiometry drives a granular superconductor-to-insulator transition while leaving the superconducting onset intact. This half-dome structure is consistent with the contrasting roles played by interstitial oxygen versus oxygen vacancies—namely, the dominance of doping versus scattering. Notably, the half-dome emerges consistently across samples with different rare-earth combinations, with or without alkaline-earth doping, revealing a general feature of the bilayer nickelate phase diagram and informing opportunities for further enhancing superconductivity.

more.title: Vinylcyclopropanes in Rearrangement Reactions
more.abstract: Vinylcyclopropanes constitute highly versatile, strained building blocks whose unique reactivity has enabled the development of a broad variety of synthetically valuable rearrangement and cycloisomerization processes. Over more than six decades of development, vinylcyclopropane chemistry has undergone remarkable evolution, particularly in recent years. Accordingly, these transformations have emerged as powerful tools for the generation of molecular complexity through strain-release-driven reaction manifolds involving both homolytic and heterolytic bond-cleavage mechanistic pathways. This Review provides a comprehensive account of the current state of the art in vinylcyclopropane rearrangement chemistry, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic principles governing these transformations and on their synthetic applications in modern organic synthesis. The different rearrangement modes accessible to vinylcyclopropane derivatives are discussed, including stereomutation processes, vinylcyclopropane-cyclopentene rearrangements, divinylcyclopropane-cycloheptadiene rearrangements, vinylcyclopropane-to-skipped-1,4-diene rearrangements, and cycloisomerization reactions involving specifically functionalized vinylcyclopropane substrates. Particular attention is devoted to the influence of substrate structure, stereochemical features, catalyst design, and thermodynamic and kinetic factors on reaction outcome, in terms of efficiency and selectivity. The broad applicability of these transformations in the synthesis of structurally sophisticated carbo- and heterocyclic architectures, including natural-product-related targets, is highlighted together with current limitations and future opportunities for the continued development of vinylcyclopropane chemistry.

more.title: Antifreeze proteins in action: structural determinants, hydration dynamics, and ice-binding mechanisms
more.abstract: Antifreeze proteins (AFPs) constitute a broad class of biological macromolecules that extend the lifespan of various organisms, including bacteria, fungi, algae, diatoms, plants, insects, and fish, by inhibiting ice growth under extreme icy conditions. We discuss the molecular mechanisms behind the specificity of AFPs in recognizing a particular water polymorph, "ice", preventing recrystallization and regulating ice growth, emphasizing their irreversible adsorption onto ice. Various structural motifs, ice-recognition mechanisms underlying antifreeze activity, and factors that enhance their antifreeze function are explained. In synergy with experimental structural biology techniques, advanced computational methods have played an essential role in elucidating the correlations among structure, protein hydration dynamics, and the functions of different classes of AFPs. In particular, advances in water-model development, improvements in sampling techniques, and free-energy calculations enable us to elucidate the origin of the unusual hydration dynamics of this group of proteins, which are crucial for ice recognition. This review discusses how molecular modeling and advanced molecular dynamics simulations shape our understanding of key aspects of AFP-mediated inhibition of ice growth. The findings presented herein can form the basis for designing AFP-inspired materials and their synthetic mimetics to regulate ice formation, which possess immense potential in the cryopreservation of biological cells, tissues, and different organs; the storage and delivery of perishable foods; the freeze-thaw degradation of cement-based substances; and the advancement of surfaces designed to prevent ice accumulation for aerospace vehicle, solar panel, and wind applications.

more.title: In-field crop disease surveillance: from phenotypes to molecules
more.abstract: Climate change and increasing ecological complexity intensify crop diseases, causing severe yield losses and threatening global food security. Timely and accurate in-field surveillance is essential for early warning and effective management of crop diseases. Advances in sensing technologies, flexible electronics, and synthetic biology are transforming crop disease surveillance from phenotypes to molecules. In this review, we first summarize major crop pathogens and pests as well as their associated disease biomarkers. We then examine field-deployable molecular detection approaches, including point-of-need assays, drone-equipped platforms, wearable devices, and sentinel plants, which enable in-field, real-time, broad-scale, and long-term surveillance of crop infection. We assess their technological readiness and applications in early crop infection detection, field pathogen survey, pesticide application instruction, and investigations of crop stress responses. Finally, we discuss the prospects of miniaturized, high-throughput analytical devices and the Internet of Things, as well as the challenges of translating in-field surveillance technologies into agricultural applications that will reshape crop disease management.

more.title: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Single-Atom Catalysis
more.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) promise control of heterogeneous reactivity at a molecular level by maximizing metal utilization and enabling deliberate tuning of local coordination and microenvironment. Yet SACs expose a central challenge in modern catalysis: the catalytically relevant site is often a working-state ensemble whose coordination, charge, spin state, adsorbate binding, and environment evolve under operating conditions. As the field expands toward bimetallic motifs, atom pairs, and hybrid SAC–nanoparticle architectures, multiple site families can coexist and interconvert. This complicates unambiguous site assignment and limits general structure–property relationships. This Review offers a critical mechanistic perspective on the use of single atoms in thermal catalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. We first summarize stabilization strategies for host matrices, emphasizing how anchoring motifs and microenvironments govern site identity and its evolution. We then develop an evidence-based approach to site assignment that treats characterization as hypothesis testing and clarifies what can and cannot be concluded regarding coordination, electronic structure, site density, and working-state identity. Finally, we connect recurring descriptors to reactivity, selectivity, and durability. We thereby highlight benchmarking techniques, site-retention metrics, and durability protocols. The goals are reliable comparison of results across studies and the transition from empirical optimization to rational design of single-atom active sites.

more.title: Visualizing spin-polarization of an altermagnet KV 2 Se 2 O via spin-selective tunneling
more.abstract: Altermagnetism, a recently identified magnetic phase that combines vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, challenges the conventional dichotomy between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. While several candidate materials have been proposed, microscopic experimental evidence linking crystal symmetry, electronic structure and d-wave spin polarization remains scarce. Here we report spin-sensitive tunneling and quasiparticle-interference (QPI) measurements on the metallic surface altermagnet KV2Se2O. Using an SmB6-nanowire tip, we observe a temperature-dependent phase contrast of impurity-induced Friedel oscillations and a bias-dependent reversal of the raw-FFT QPI anisotropy between the qx and qy channels. The W-tip controls instead show mostly in-phase oscillations and a non-sign-reversing QPI anisotropy. Together with numerical simulations, these observations support momentum-dependent spin polarization that follows a characteristic d-wave form factor. Our results establish KV2Se2O as a material platform to study the interplay between spin-valley locking, Fermi-surface instability and unconventional magnetism, and highlight spin-selective tunneling as a local probe of compensated magnetic spin textures.

more.title: Mpemba effect in a two-dimensional bistable potential
more.abstract: We present an exactly solvable model of the Mpemba effect in an overdamped Langevin system confined to a two-dimensional, radially symmetric bistable potential. The potential is constructed as a piecewise quadratic-logarithmic function that is continuous and differentiable at the matching radii, enabling an exact mapping of the corresponding Fokker-Planck operator to a Schrödinger-type eigenvalue problem. The relaxation spectrum and eigenmodes are obtained analytically in each region in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, with eigenvalues determined from matching conditions. % Focusing on isotropic equilibrium initial states at inverse temperature βᵢₙᵢ quenched to a bath at inverse temperature β, we derive explicit expressions for the mode amplitudes governing long-time relaxation. We demonstrate that the coefficient of the slowest mode exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on βᵢₙᵢ and identify a sufficient crossing condition for the Kullback-Leibler divergence in terms of the two slowest modes, if the global minimum of the potential is located far away from the origin and the second minimum exists near the origin. For corresponding parameters, we demonstrate that the Mpemba effect can be realized. % Our results provide a rare example of an analytically tractable two-dimensional model exhibiting anomalous relaxation without any confining walls, extending previous one-dimensional constructions with a hard wall and clarifying the role of radial geometry in nonequilibrium relaxation phenomena.

more.title: Spin-Resolved Microscopy of Sr 87 SU ( N ) Fermi-Hubbard Systems
more.abstract: Quantum-gas microscopes provide direct access to the phases of the Hubbard model, bringing microscopic insight into the complex competition between interactions, SU(2) magnetism, and doping. Alkaline-earth(-like) fermions extend this spin- 1 / 2 paradigm by realizing higher symmetries and giving access to SU ( N ) Hubbard models, with rich phase diagrams to be unveiled. Despite its fundamental interest, a microscopic exploration of SU ( N ) quantum systems has remained elusive. Here, we report the realization of a quantum-gas microscope for fermionic Sr 87 . Our imaging scheme, based on cooling and fluorescence on the narrow intercombination line at 689 nm, enables spin-resolved single-atom detection. By implementing a spin-selective optical pumping protocol, we determine the occupation of each of the ten spin states in a single experimental realization, a crucial capability for probing site-resolved magnetic correlations. We benchmark our method by observing single-particle Larmor precession across the full spin- 9 / 2 ground-state manifold and use numerical simulations of SU ( N ) Fermi-Hubbard chains, incorporating the measured detection fidelities, to demonstrate its capability to resolve many-body spin correlations. Our results establish Sr 87 quantum-gas microscopy as a powerful approach to study exotic magnetism in the SU ( N ) Fermi-Hubbard model and provide a detection tool for studies in quantum simulation, computation, and metrology.

more.title: GA-NIFS: A post-starburst main sequence disk galaxy undergoing ordered rotation at z = 4.26
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Rotating galaxies with relaxed gaseous disks have been discovered across cosmic time, from the local Universe to high redshift. But few such sources have been confirmed at z > 4, making them a precious sample to examine the conditions required for such ordered kinematics in an early, more chaotic Universe. One of the best examples of this sample is the galaxy DLA0817g1 (z = 4.2603), which shows remarkably clear rotation in ALMA [C ii] data. We present JWST/NIRSpec IFU data (R ∼ 2700) of DLA0817g1, which we combine with archival ALMA [C ii] observations to place constraints on its ISM conditions and morpho-kinematics. From a combination of line ratios, we find a high gas-phase metallicity (Zgas ∼ 0.8 Z⊙), high fraction of obscured star formation, low ionisation (compared to other high-redshift galaxies observed with JWST), and no significant evidence for AGN. Dynamical modelling with ^(3D)Barolo reveals nearly identical rotation in Hα and [C ii]. Using our metallicity estimate and previous CO and [C ii] detections, we derive a new estimate of the molecular gas mass, relieving a previous strain in the mass budget. Altogether, we suggest that this is a post-burst, main-sequence galaxy, where high levels of past star formation resulted in significant chemical enrichment (i.e., Zgas and Mdust), but the current activity is lower (i.e., lower ionisation parameter and lack of starburst activity). These new observations have opened a window into the interplay of gas, metallicity, star formation, and kinematics in a prototypical early disk galaxy.

more.title: Quasar Impostors: Two Extremely UV-Bright ( M UV ≈ −23.5) Reionisation-Epoch Galaxies Powered by Very Massive Stars
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: The extreme bright end of the galaxy UV luminosity function during reionisation remains poorly constrained, particularly where the galaxy and quasar luminosity functions overlap and source classification becomes ambiguous. We present JWST/NIRSpec and ALMA Band-6 observations of J1450−0144 (z = 6.627) and J1429−0104 (z = 6.796), two MUV ≃ −23.5 sources originally classified as faint quasars by SHELLQs. NIRSpec reveals blue UV continua, strong P Cygni profiles in N v, Si iv, and C iv, broad He ii λ1640 emission with rest-frame equivalent widths of 8.8 ± 1.2 and 3.7 ± 1.1 Å, respectively, and narrow nebular lines, reclassifying both as extremely UV-luminous galaxies. Standard population-synthesis models cannot simultaneously reproduce the strong He ii and wind features, whereas models incorporating very massive stars (VMS; M ≳ 100 M⊙) with dedicated wind prescriptions can. These models favor a star-formation duration of 2–4 Myr for J1450−0144, with a broader allowed range for J1429−0104, stellar masses of log (M⋆/M⊙) ≈ 9.2–9.9, and star-formation rates of ≃ 300–540 M⊙ yr−1. Under the same VMS wind models, equivalent-width diagnostics imply Mup ≳ 225 M⊙ for J1429−0104, while J1450−0144 lies beyond even the Mup = 475 M⊙ grid. ALMA detects luminous [C ii] 158 μm emission in both systems, with L[CII] ≈ 0.8 and 4.1 × 109 L⊙, respectively. J1429−0104 additionally shows bright dust continuum, with both [C ii] and dust offset by ∼5.4 kpc from its UV emission. These sources demonstrate that VMS can power some of the most UV-luminous galaxies at cosmic dawn and show that source classifications, and hence the inferred demographics of both galaxies and quasars in the crossover regime, need revisiting.

more.title: Transforming molecular evolutionary analyses with protein foundation models
Turbulent gas-rich discs at high redshift: the origin of early massive stellar bars
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Recent observations combining the power of ALMA and JWST inter alia have revealed large (3 − 7 kpc), massive (3 − 10 × 1010 M⊙) stellar bars at z = 4 − 5 when the Universe was only 1.2-1.6 Gyr old. At this early epoch, the host galaxy was baryon-dominated (typically 75% gas, 25% stars) within the observed extent of the disc (8 − 15 kpc). Using Nexus N-body/hydrodynamic simulations, we show that such bars can form promptly (400−800 Myr), provided the disc mass fraction is high (fdisc ≳ 70%) and the bar is gas-dominated at the time of its formation, consistent with the observations. In this limit, gas-free bars form more slowly (≈1 Gyr) and are weakened by vertical bending modes, but a substantial gas component suppresses this instability. Unlike massive bars in the local Universe, these early bars were sites of vigorous star formation, as we show. Remarkably, for gas-rich models with fgas ≲ 60%, the bars develop X-shaped boxy bulges; at higher gas fractions (fgas > 60%), diffusion suppresses resonant orbit trapping and the emerging bar collapses within 1 Gyr to form a classical bulge. The bar formation time, length, mass, and m = 2 Fourier amplitude are all inversely related to fgas. We present a simple analytic model for how stochastic forcing shifts the bar onset time, defined as the time at which the growing bar amplitude reaches a specified threshold.

more.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τα∝B−2. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 1012 G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

more.title: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial
more.abstract: Incretin mimetics as obesity therapy induce substantial weight and fat loss but also decrease lean soft tissue mass, possibly impairing skeletal muscle function. Here, in this two-arm randomized controlled trial of adding resistance exercise (REx) to tirzepatide (T), 120 adults with overweight or obesity were treated with tirzepatide and randomized to thrice-weekly resistance exercise training or usual activities for 40 weeks. Tirzepatide was safe, and most participants tolerated up-titration to 15 mg weekly. Adherence to resistance exercise was 91%. Weight loss achieved was similar (T = -22.61 kg, T+REx = -22.28 kg, P = 0.694). For primary outcomes, loss of total fat mass was similar (T = -17.19 kg, T+REx = -17.98 kg, P = 0.700; between-group difference = -0.77 kg, 95% confidence interval (CI): -2.14 kg to 0.60 kg), but resistance exercise reduced loss of total lean soft tissue mass (T = -4.67 kg, T+REx = -3.57 kg, P < 0.001; between-group difference = 1.09 kg, 95% CI: 0.43-1.75 kg). For related endpoints, resistance exercise reduced loss of appendicular lean soft tissue mass (T = -3.55 kg, T+REx = -2.92 kg, P < 0.001). Upper and lower body muscle strength decreased with tirzepatide (bench press -4.09 kg, lat pulldown -4.42 kg, knee extension -4.42 kg) but increased with T+REx (+4.68 kg, +8.58 kg, +5.88 kg, respectively, all P < 0.001 versus tirzepatide). In conclusion, resistance exercise training attenuated loss of total lean soft tissue mass, representing an effective adjunct to tirzepatide anti-obesity therapy. more.title: Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS Randomized Clinical Trial
more.abstract: Importance: Information on the effects of tirzepatide, a once-weekly glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist approved for obesity management in adults with obesity, remains limited in adolescents. Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly tirzepatide in adolescents with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication. Design, Setting, and Participants: This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, 72-week clinical trial was conducted at 31 medical research centers and hospitals in Canada, the Czech Republic, Israel, Italy, Poland, and the US from October 16, 2023, to June 2, 2026, among adolescents aged 12 years to younger than 18 years with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication. Interventions: Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide, escalated to a maximum tolerated dose (5, 10, or 15 mg), or placebo for 72 weeks, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary end point was percent change in body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) from baseline to week 72. Key secondary end points included percentages of participants achieving BMI reductions of at least 5%, at least 10%, at least 15%, and at least 20%; changes in BMI SD score; BMI expressed as a percentage of the 95th percentile; and body weight, waist circumference, and physical functioning from baseline to week 72. Safety outcomes included treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events. more.title: Enhancing Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning via Hierarchical Feature Optimization
more.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
more.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a compelling paradigm for privacy-preserving distributed machine learning, allowing multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model by transmitting locally computed gradients to a central server without exposing their private data. Nonetheless, recent studies find that the gradients exchanged in the FL system are also vulnerable to privacy leakage, e.g., an attacker can invert shared gradients to reconstruct sensitive data by leveraging pre-trained generative adversarial networks (GAN) as prior knowledge. However, existing attacks simply perform gradient inversion in the latent space of the GAN model, which limits their expression ability and generalizability. To tackle these challenges, we propose Gradient Inversion over Feature Domains (GIFD), which disassembles the GAN model and searches the hierarchical features of the intermediate layers. Instead of optimizing only over the initial latent code, we progressively change the optimized layer, from the initial latent space to intermediate layers closer to the output images. In addition, we design a regularizer to avoid unreal image generation by adding a small l₁ ball constraint to the searching range. We also extend GIFD to the out-of-distribution (OOD) setting, which weakens the assumption that the training sets of GANs and FL tasks obey the same data distribution. Furthermore, we consider the challenging OOD scenario of label inconsistency and propose a label mapping technique as an effective solution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve high-quality reconstruction and outperform competitive baselines across a variety of FL scenarios.

more.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
more.abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain’s proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is, for example, 1,2^(1/3),2^(-1/3) 1 , 2 1 / 3 , 2 − 1 / 3 . This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature (2,2) ( 2 , 2 ) . The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature (3,3) ( 3 , 3 ) in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on SL(2,Z)³ SL(2, R)³ SL ( 2 , Z ) 3 ∖ SL ( 2 , R ) 3 over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner’s measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

more.title: Burst Spiking Neural Networks
more.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
more.abstract: A central goal of current Spiking Neural Network (SNN) research is to improve their accuracy toward becoming low-power alternatives to Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). This work further argues that realizing this ambition requires improving not only accuracy but also robustness, defined as the ability to maintain correct predictions under input perturbations. We identify two key issues in existing SNN methods that undermine robustness. First, binary spiking activations can produce large activation-state changes under small perturbations. Second, the lack of effective weight constraints makes network outputs more sensitive to input variations. To this end, we propose Burst Spiking Neural Networks (BuSNNs), built upon Burst-enhanced Spiking Neurons (BSNs) and a Dynamic Weight Constraint (DWC) mechanism. BSNs incorporate burst firing to provide a graded spiking pattern. This spiking mechanism mitigates perturbation-induced transitions in activation states and thereby enhances robustness. DWC penalizes connection weights based on activation states, effectively reducing weight magnitudes and improving robustness while preserving accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses to support these robustness effects. Experimental results further show that, on smaller-scale benchmarks such as CIFAR-10, BuSNNs outperform both SNN and ANN counterparts in accuracy and robustness. On large-scale ImageNet, BuSNN with the MS ResNet-34 backbone further improves top-1 accuracy and corruption robustness over the corresponding SNN baseline by 3.18% and 2.66%, respectively. Despite using spike-based activations, BuSNNs surpass 4-bit activation-quantized ANN baselines and approach 8-bit ANN baselines on ImageNet. They also preserve SNNs' low-power advantage with up to a 4.38× theoretical energy…

more.title: A Plasma eMTBR-Tau Immunoassay for Detection of Advanced Insoluble Tau Pathology
more.abstract: Importance: Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation. Objective: To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET). Design, Setting, and Participants: This cross-sectional study included brain donors with antemortem plasma from 2 US autopsy cohorts, and individuals with plasma samples and tau PET from 2 imaging cohorts in Canada and Sweden, with visits between 2002 and 2025 depending on the cohort. Exposures: Plasma eMTBR-tau measured with an immunoassay and eMTBR-tau243 measured with mass spectrometry. Main Outcomes and Measures: Plasma eMTBR-tau levels across neuropathologic Braak neurofibrillary tangle stages (I-VI, ranging from tangles confined to the entorhinal region to widespread neocortical tangles) and tau-PET Braak stages (0-VI), expressed as fold changes. Correlations with regional tau-PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs; higher values indicating more tau tangles), discrimination of regional tau-PET positivity (area under the curve [AUC]), and correlation with mass spectrometry-based eMTBR-tau243. more.title: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4+ T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity
more.abstract: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4 + T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (T FH ) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 ( Tnfaip3 ) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating T FH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

shortlist.title: Airy functions from quantum M-theory
shortlist.abstract: We show that Airy function partition functions for M2-brane theories may be derived from relative equivariant localization of quantum M-theory. The eleven-dimensional Chern–Simons coupling gives the cubic term in the grand potential, while the X 8 correction gives the charge shift. Fixing the M2-brane charge turns the localized M-theory path integral into an Airy integral. In this way we derive the ABJM result, its toric Calabi–Yau generalizations, and gravitational blocks for black holes and other spacetimes, up to the prefactor and non-perturbative corrections.

shortlist.title: The Explosion Time of the Jittering Jet Explosion Mechanism (JJEM)
shortlist.abstract: We compare the expected explosion time of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) to that in the neutrino-driven (the delayed neutrino) mechanism, and conclude that for most, but not all, stellar models, even when the neutrino-driven mechanism might have led to an explosion, the JJEM starts to operate before the neutrino mechanism fully revives the stalled shock. To achieve this goal, we conduct comprehensive one-dimensional stellar evolution simulations using the code mesa to determine the expected explosion time according to the JJEM, which corresponds to the time when the inner convective layer of the core is accreted onto the newly born neutron star (NS). We present results for many hydrogen-rich, hydrogen-stripped, and helium+hydrogen-stripped envelope CCSN progenitor models. We find that most, but not all, of our models in the initial mass range of M ZAMS = 12 M ⊙ to M ZAMS = 40 M ⊙ , have at least one strong convective zone inside the mass coordinate that is the maximum baryonic mass of an NS, m ≃ 2.65 M ⊙ , which can facilitate the JJEM. This study contributes to establishing the JJEM as a viable explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

shortlist.title: Lattice QCD determination of the γ Z box contribution to the proton weak charge
shortlist.abstract: We present the first lattice QCD determination of the γ Z box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, ▫ γ Z , a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to E = 155 MeV. At E = 0 , the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain ▫ γ Z ( 0 ) = 0.00411 ( 9 ) . Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of Q W p = 0.06987 ( 50 ) . The calculated energy dependence of ▫ γ Z is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract Q W p . Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the γ Z box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.

shortlist.title: Muon Lifetime and Fermi Constant: An Update
shortlist.abstract: We present an updated prediction for the lifetime of the muon, including a detailed analysis of all relevant uncertainties. Our prediction includes QED corrections up to order α 3 and state-of-the-art hadronic contributions based on dispersive methods. Radiative corrections and finite-electron-mass effects are parametrized by the correction factor Δ q in τ μ − 1 = G F 2 m μ 5 ( 1 + Δ q ) / ( 192 π 3 ) , for which we obtain Δ q = ( − 4 384 700 ± 34 ) × 10 − 9 . This reduces the uncertainty associated with Δ q by an order of magnitude compared to the previous prediction at order α 2 . We use our results to provide an updated value of the Fermi coupling constant, G F = 1.166 378 60 ( 59 ) × 10 − 5 GeV − 2 (consistent with the current Particle Data Group estimate). Further improvements will require better measurements of the muon lifetime and mass.

shortlist.title: A New Bayesian Framework with Mass–Radius–Space Priors to Constrain the Neutron Star Equation of State
shortlist.abstract: We propose a new Bayesian framework to infer the neutron star equation of state (EOS) from mass and radius observations and neutron matter theory by defining priors that directly parameterize mass–radius space instead of pressure–energy density space. We use direct and accurate inversion approximations to map mass–radius relations to the underlying EOS. We systematically compare its EOS inferences with those inferred from traditional EOS parameterizations, taking care to quantify the systematic prior uncertainties of both. Our results show that prior uncertainties should be included in all Bayesian approaches. The alternative framework provides broader and more uniform coverage of the physically allowed mass–radius space, especially small radius configurations, with enhanced computational efficiency. Substantially reduced dependence on prior choices seems to result from having both prior and posterior distributions in the same observational mass–radius space. Results indicate that direct parameterization in observed space offers a robust and efficient alternative to traditional methods.

shortlist.title: MAGNUS. III. Mild Evolution of the Total Density Slope in Massive Early-type Galaxies Since z ∼ 1 from Dynamical Modeling of MUSE Integral-field Stellar Kinematics
shortlist.abstract: We investigate the total mass density slope evolution in massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) over the last 6.5 Gyr (0 < z < 0.75). We perform a detailed dynamical analysis of approximately 200 ETGs spanning the redshift range of 0.24 < z < 0.75, utilizing spatially resolved stellar kinematics derived from high signal-to-noise ratio MUSE-DEEP spectroscopy and surface brightness models from high-resolution Hubble Space Telescope imaging. We constrain mass distributions using the Jeans anisotropic modeling technique coupled with the multi-Gaussian expansion method. To rigorously constrain evolutionary trends, we combine this intermediate-redshift data set with a local ETG sample ( z ∼ 0.05) from the MaNGA survey. We adopt dynamical constraints for the local sample derived using an identical homogeneous methodology, ensuring a strictly consistent comparison. We found that the total density profiles of the intermediate-redshift ETG sample are approximately isothermal and exhibit a median mass-weighted total density slope, γ T = 2.19 ± 0.01 at z = 0.44 , which is shallower than the local baseline of γ T = 2.26 ± 0.01 at z = 0.04 . This structural shift corresponds to a redshift gradient of d γ T / d z ≈ −0.20 ± 0.03, detected at ∼6 σ significance. We demonstrate that this trend is robust against model assumptions and persists even when restricting the analysis to high-velocity dispersion systems ( σ e > 150 km s −1 ). Our findings are consistent with previous lensing-based studies and in tension with cosmological simulations. The observed steepening suggests that dissipative processes, such as gas-rich accretion and mergers, must play a nonnegligible role in the late-stage assembly of massive ETGs.

shortlist.title: High-temperature η -pairing superconductivity in the photodoped Hubbard model
shortlist.abstract: We investigate superconductivity emerging in the photodoped Mott insulating Hubbard model using steady-state dynamical mean-field theory implemented on the real-frequency axis. By employing high-order strong-coupling impurity solvers, we obtain the nonequilibrium phase diagram for photoinduced η -pairing superconductivity with a remarkably high effective critical temperature. We further identify a superconducting gap in the momentum-resolved spectral function and optical conductivity, providing spectroscopic signatures accessible to experiments. Our results highlight a route to a controllable form of high-temperature superconductivity in nonequilibrium strongly correlated systems, fundamentally distinct from the equilibrium s -wave pairing state in the attractive Hubbard model or cuprate-like d -wave superconductors.

shortlist.title: Reaching for the Edge. II. Stellar Halos out to Large Radii as a Tracer of Dark Matter Halo Mass
shortlist.abstract: The diffuse outskirts of brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) encode valuable information about the assembly history and mass of their host dark matter halos. However, the low surface brightness of these stellar halos has historically made them difficult to observe. Recent deep imaging, particularly with Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC), has shown that the stellar mass within large projected annuli, such as 50 and 100 kpc, is a promising proxy for halo mass. However, the optimal radial definition of this “outskirt mass” remains uncertain. We construct an HSC-like mock observing pipeline to measure stellar mass density profiles of BCGs in the IllustrisTNG simulations. The resulting profiles reproduce HSC profiles across 6 orders of magnitude in surface density. We then measure stellar masses within different annuli and how tightly they connect to halo mass. Stellar masses measured within simple apertures exhibit more scatter in the stellar mass–halo mass relation than those measured within projected ellipsoidal annuli. We identify an optimal range, with inner radii of ∼60–300 kpc and outer radii of ∼250–500 kpc. We also introduce two halo-mass-dependent Sérsic models for average stellar halo profiles. The first depends only on halo mass, M vir , and has a median error of 0.19 dex (∼54%). Adding the central stellar mass of the BCG as a second parameter reduces this to 0.15 dex (∼39%). Together, these results provide fitting functions for BCG stellar halos that can be applied to future wide-field surveys to infer halo masses from deep imaging data.
