shortlist.title: Discerning between Excimer and Singlet Fission Sites Using Modulated Magnetic Field Photoluminescence
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Magnetic field effects play a key role in the characterization of organic electronic materials. In particular, the microscopic processes underlying singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation have been clarified in recent years through the observation and subsequent theoretical explanation of magnetic field effects in these processes. Here, we study magnetic field effects on the luminescence of 5,12-bis((triisopropylsilyl)ethynyl)tetracene, a well-studied material in which both singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation occur. By performing highly sensitive modulated-field magneto-photoluminescence experiments we observe magnetic field effect lineshapes with rich detail, allowing a precise characterization of triplet exciton dynamics. By additionally filtering these magnetic field effects by luminescence wavelength, we can identify the excimer state by its unique magnetic field signature. Finally, we show that a theoretical explanation of these field effects requires a model that explicitly accounts for quantum coherences, which highlights the importance of detailed spin dynamics modeling in understanding magnetic field effects, even at room temperature.

shortlist.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
shortlist.abstract: Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense 5 .

shortlist.title: Enhancing Grignard Reactions via Anion Borrowing in Deep Eutectic/Organic Biphasic Media
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as powerful reaction media to enhance nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules. In this protocol, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i-PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results demonstrate enhanced chemoselectivity for the Grignard addition over β-H transfer side reaction from the isopropyl group when in DES/THF. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the neutral Grignard species in neat THF kinetically favors β-H transfer, chloride enrichment from the DES renders both pathways kinetically competitive and markedly increases the thermodynamic preference for the addition product through enhanced intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these nonconventional solvents.

Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
shortlist.abstract: One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics…

A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
shortlist.abstract: Wernicke's area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke's area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke's area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

shortlist.title: 1,8-Azulenedicarboxylic Imides: Excited-State Properties and Catalytic Activity of a Nonalternant π-System
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Imide-functionalized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) represent an important class of π-conjugated molecules; however, their nonalternant isomers remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis and investigation of the structural, photophysical, and excited-state properties of 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides as nonalternant isomers of 1,8-naphthalimides. These compounds retain the characteristic photophysics of the azulene framework, including near-infrared (NIR) absorption and anti-Kasha emission, while substitution at the imide nitrogen enables modulation of their excited-state electronic structures. QD-NEVPT2 calculations identified an S2–T1 pair with relatively large SOC and LE-to-CT character, suggesting a plausible ISC pathway associated with the observed singlet-oxygen photosensitization. Consequently, 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides function as an effective visible-light photocatalyst for the α-cyanation of secondary and tertiary amines. These findings demonstrate that the present nonalternant molecular design provides a strategy for tuning excited-state properties by modulating locally excited and charge-transfer states in imide chromophores.

shortlist.title: Composition-Driven Discovery of Multimetallic Catalysts Using Features Inspired by the Virtual Crystal Approximation
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Structure–activity relationships built on structure-derived descriptors are a dominant paradigm in catalyst screening. However, this structure-driven framework scales poorly to multimetallic systems, where active sites are heterogeneous, dynamically reconstruct under operating conditions, and require extensive structural enumeration and system-specific descriptor engineering. Here, we introduce a composition-driven screening strategy for multimetallic catalysts using feature construction inspired by the virtual crystal approximation. Specifically, multimetallic sites are represented as composition-weighted pseudoatoms, allowing readily available elemental properties to be converted into predictive features without explicit structural modeling. Unlike elemental fractions alone, these features encode physicochemical differences among the constituent metals. We demonstrate this approach using Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) as a compositionally tunable and reconstruction-prone validation platform for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Combining the composition-derived features with symbolic regression yields an explicit expression for ranking compositions, guiding experimental identification of four high-performance PBAs. We further evaluate this strategy across six literature data sets spanning different catalyst families and reactions, independently training a model for each. Using one of the models, we screen and experimentally validate a perovskite catalyst achieving an overpotential of 189 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in acidic OER. These results demonstrate the broad applicability of virtual crystal approximation-inspired feature construction for composition-driven screening of multimetallic catalysts.

shortlist.title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
shortlist.abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

shortlist.title: Fixing the power transmission crisis
shortlist.abstract: Experimentation, learning, and existing regulatory and technology options could help align stakeholders.

shortlist.title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation
shortlist.abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron-containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

shortlist.title: Superconducting Half-Dome in Bilayer Nickelates
shortlist.abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges and collapses in correlated electron systems remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics. As a recently discovered member of the high temperature superconductor family, bilayer nickelates provide a new opportunity for examining this problem. Their pronounced sensitivity to oxygen stoichiometry, while posing challenges for stabilizing superconductivity, simultaneously offers an effective control parameter for tuning electronic phases. Here we report a superconducting half-dome in compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films as a function of continuous tuning of oxygen stoichiometry. Starting from an optimally superconducting state, increasing oxygen stoichiometry gradually suppresses superconductivity toward a metallic phase, whereas decreasing oxygen stoichiometry drives a granular superconductor-to-insulator transition while leaving the superconducting onset intact. This half-dome structure is consistent with the contrasting roles played by interstitial oxygen versus oxygen vacancies—namely, the dominance of doping versus scattering. Notably, the half-dome emerges consistently across samples with different rare-earth combinations, with or without alkaline-earth doping, revealing a general feature of the bilayer nickelate phase diagram and informing opportunities for further enhancing superconductivity.

shortlist.title: Vinylcyclopropanes in Rearrangement Reactions
shortlist.abstract: Vinylcyclopropanes constitute highly versatile, strained building blocks whose unique reactivity has enabled the development of a broad variety of synthetically valuable rearrangement and cycloisomerization processes. Over more than six decades of development, vinylcyclopropane chemistry has undergone remarkable evolution, particularly in recent years. Accordingly, these transformations have emerged as powerful tools for the generation of molecular complexity through strain-release-driven reaction manifolds involving both homolytic and heterolytic bond-cleavage mechanistic pathways. This Review provides a comprehensive account of the current state of the art in vinylcyclopropane rearrangement chemistry, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic principles governing these transformations and on their synthetic applications in modern organic synthesis. The different rearrangement modes accessible to vinylcyclopropane derivatives are discussed, including stereomutation processes, vinylcyclopropane-cyclopentene rearrangements, divinylcyclopropane-cycloheptadiene rearrangements, vinylcyclopropane-to-skipped-1,4-diene rearrangements, and cycloisomerization reactions involving specifically functionalized vinylcyclopropane substrates. Particular attention is devoted to the influence of substrate structure, stereochemical features, catalyst design, and thermodynamic and kinetic factors on reaction outcome, in terms of efficiency and selectivity. The broad applicability of these transformations in the synthesis of structurally sophisticated carbo- and heterocyclic architectures, including natural-product-related targets, is highlighted together with current limitations and future opportunities for the continued development of vinylcyclopropane chemistry.

shortlist.title: Antifreeze proteins in action: structural determinants, hydration dynamics, and ice-binding mechanisms
shortlist.abstract: Antifreeze proteins (AFPs) constitute a broad class of biological macromolecules that extend the lifespan of various organisms, including bacteria, fungi, algae, diatoms, plants, insects, and fish, by inhibiting ice growth under extreme icy conditions. We discuss the molecular mechanisms behind the specificity of AFPs in recognizing a particular water polymorph, "ice", preventing recrystallization and regulating ice growth, emphasizing their irreversible adsorption onto ice. Various structural motifs, ice-recognition mechanisms underlying antifreeze activity, and factors that enhance their antifreeze function are explained. In synergy with experimental structural biology techniques, advanced computational methods have played an essential role in elucidating the correlations among structure, protein hydration dynamics, and the functions of different classes of AFPs. In particular, advances in water-model development, improvements in sampling techniques, and free-energy calculations enable us to elucidate the origin of the unusual hydration dynamics of this group of proteins, which are crucial for ice recognition. This review discusses how molecular modeling and advanced molecular dynamics simulations shape our understanding of key aspects of AFP-mediated inhibition of ice growth. The findings presented herein can form the basis for designing AFP-inspired materials and their synthetic mimetics to regulate ice formation, which possess immense potential in the cryopreservation of biological cells, tissues, and different organs; the storage and delivery of perishable foods; the freeze-thaw degradation of cement-based substances; and the advancement of surfaces designed to prevent ice accumulation for aerospace vehicle, solar panel, and wind applications.

shortlist.title: In-field crop disease surveillance: from phenotypes to molecules
shortlist.abstract: Climate change and increasing ecological complexity intensify crop diseases, causing severe yield losses and threatening global food security. Timely and accurate in-field surveillance is essential for early warning and effective management of crop diseases. Advances in sensing technologies, flexible electronics, and synthetic biology are transforming crop disease surveillance from phenotypes to molecules. In this review, we first summarize major crop pathogens and pests as well as their associated disease biomarkers. We then examine field-deployable molecular detection approaches, including point-of-need assays, drone-equipped platforms, wearable devices, and sentinel plants, which enable in-field, real-time, broad-scale, and long-term surveillance of crop infection. We assess their technological readiness and applications in early crop infection detection, field pathogen survey, pesticide application instruction, and investigations of crop stress responses. Finally, we discuss the prospects of miniaturized, high-throughput analytical devices and the Internet of Things, as well as the challenges of translating in-field surveillance technologies into agricultural applications that will reshape crop disease management.

shortlist.title: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Single-Atom Catalysis
shortlist.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) promise control of heterogeneous reactivity at a molecular level by maximizing metal utilization and enabling deliberate tuning of local coordination and microenvironment. Yet SACs expose a central challenge in modern catalysis: the catalytically relevant site is often a working-state ensemble whose coordination, charge, spin state, adsorbate binding, and environment evolve under operating conditions. As the field expands toward bimetallic motifs, atom pairs, and hybrid SAC–nanoparticle architectures, multiple site families can coexist and interconvert. This complicates unambiguous site assignment and limits general structure–property relationships. This Review offers a critical mechanistic perspective on the use of single atoms in thermal catalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. We first summarize stabilization strategies for host matrices, emphasizing how anchoring motifs and microenvironments govern site identity and its evolution. We then develop an evidence-based approach to site assignment that treats characterization as hypothesis testing and clarifies what can and cannot be concluded regarding coordination, electronic structure, site density, and working-state identity. Finally, we connect recurring descriptors to reactivity, selectivity, and durability. We thereby highlight benchmarking techniques, site-retention metrics, and durability protocols. The goals are reliable comparison of results across studies and the transition from empirical optimization to rational design of single-atom active sites.

shortlist.title: Visualizing spin-polarization of an altermagnet KV 2 Se 2 O via spin-selective tunneling
shortlist.abstract: Altermagnetism, a recently identified magnetic phase that combines vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, challenges the conventional dichotomy between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. While several candidate materials have been proposed, microscopic experimental evidence linking crystal symmetry, electronic structure and d-wave spin polarization remains scarce. Here we report spin-sensitive tunneling and quasiparticle-interference (QPI) measurements on the metallic surface altermagnet KV2Se2O. Using an SmB6-nanowire tip, we observe a temperature-dependent phase contrast of impurity-induced Friedel oscillations and a bias-dependent reversal of the raw-FFT QPI anisotropy between the qx and qy channels. The W-tip controls instead show mostly in-phase oscillations and a non-sign-reversing QPI anisotropy. Together with numerical simulations, these observations support momentum-dependent spin polarization that follows a characteristic d-wave form factor. Our results establish KV2Se2O as a material platform to study the interplay between spin-valley locking, Fermi-surface instability and unconventional magnetism, and highlight spin-selective tunneling as a local probe of compensated magnetic spin textures.

shortlist.title: Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis
shortlist.abstract: Endometriosis is a painful and heterogeneous condition that affects up to one in ten women. Its genetic underpinnings remain partially unknown, and its precise disease mechanisms are yet to be elucidated. Here we report a genome-wide study of endometriosis as part of the Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative representing over 1 million participants (32% non-European ancestry). We detected 58 genomic regions (27 previously unreported) across diverse ancestry groups and new procedure-confirmed case identification algorithms. These include loci unique to African and admixed American populations. A search for genetically driven comorbidities revealed dozens of associations with known and previously uncharacterized risk factors. Then, within prioritized cellular contexts, we found numerous examples of gene expression affected by endometriosis status. Including further multiomic analyses, we implicated a total of 314 genes, suggesting multiple targets for therapeutic intervention. Our findings span molecular, cellular and phenotypic scales, highlighting interconnected pathways that underscore the multifaceted etiology of endometriosis.

shortlist.title: Mpemba effect in a two-dimensional bistable potential
shortlist.abstract: We present an exactly solvable model of the Mpemba effect in an overdamped Langevin system confined to a two-dimensional, radially symmetric bistable potential. The potential is constructed as a piecewise quadratic-logarithmic function that is continuous and differentiable at the matching radii, enabling an exact mapping of the corresponding Fokker-Planck operator to a Schrödinger-type eigenvalue problem. The relaxation spectrum and eigenmodes are obtained analytically in each region in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, with eigenvalues determined from matching conditions. % Focusing on isotropic equilibrium initial states at inverse temperature βᵢₙᵢ quenched to a bath at inverse temperature β, we derive explicit expressions for the mode amplitudes governing long-time relaxation. We demonstrate that the coefficient of the slowest mode exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on βᵢₙᵢ and identify a sufficient crossing condition for the Kullback-Leibler divergence in terms of the two slowest modes, if the global minimum of the potential is located far away from the origin and the second minimum exists near the origin. For corresponding parameters, we demonstrate that the Mpemba effect can be realized. % Our results provide a rare example of an analytically tractable two-dimensional model exhibiting anomalous relaxation without any confining walls, extending previous one-dimensional constructions with a hard wall and clarifying the role of radial geometry in nonequilibrium relaxation phenomena.

shortlist.title: Spin-Resolved Microscopy of Sr 87 SU ( N ) Fermi-Hubbard Systems
shortlist.abstract: Quantum-gas microscopes provide direct access to the phases of the Hubbard model, bringing microscopic insight into the complex competition between interactions, SU(2) magnetism, and doping. Alkaline-earth(-like) fermions extend this spin- 1 / 2 paradigm by realizing higher symmetries and giving access to SU ( N ) Hubbard models, with rich phase diagrams to be unveiled. Despite its fundamental interest, a microscopic exploration of SU ( N ) quantum systems has remained elusive. Here, we report the realization of a quantum-gas microscope for fermionic Sr 87 . Our imaging scheme, based on cooling and fluorescence on the narrow intercombination line at 689 nm, enables spin-resolved single-atom detection. By implementing a spin-selective optical pumping protocol, we determine the occupation of each of the ten spin states in a single experimental realization, a crucial capability for probing site-resolved magnetic correlations. We benchmark our method by observing single-particle Larmor precession across the full spin- 9 / 2 ground-state manifold and use numerical simulations of SU ( N ) Fermi-Hubbard chains, incorporating the measured detection fidelities, to demonstrate its capability to resolve many-body spin correlations. Our results establish Sr 87 quantum-gas microscopy as a powerful approach to study exotic magnetism in the SU ( N ) Fermi-Hubbard model and provide a detection tool for studies in quantum simulation, computation, and metrology.

shortlist.title: GA-NIFS: A post-starburst main sequence disk galaxy undergoing ordered rotation at z = 4.26
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Rotating galaxies with relaxed gaseous disks have been discovered across cosmic time, from the local Universe to high redshift. But few such sources have been confirmed at z > 4, making them a precious sample to examine the conditions required for such ordered kinematics in an early, more chaotic Universe. One of the best examples of this sample is the galaxy DLA0817g1 (z = 4.2603), which shows remarkably clear rotation in ALMA [C ii] data. We present JWST/NIRSpec IFU data (R ∼ 2700) of DLA0817g1, which we combine with archival ALMA [C ii] observations to place constraints on its ISM conditions and morpho-kinematics. From a combination of line ratios, we find a high gas-phase metallicity (Zgas ∼ 0.8 Z⊙), high fraction of obscured star formation, low ionisation (compared to other high-redshift galaxies observed with JWST), and no significant evidence for AGN. Dynamical modelling with ^(3D)Barolo reveals nearly identical rotation in Hα and [C ii]. Using our metallicity estimate and previous CO and [C ii] detections, we derive a new estimate of the molecular gas mass, relieving a previous strain in the mass budget. Altogether, we suggest that this is a post-burst, main-sequence galaxy, where high levels of past star formation resulted in significant chemical enrichment (i.e., Zgas and Mdust), but the current activity is lower (i.e., lower ionisation parameter and lack of starburst activity). These new observations have opened a window into the interplay of gas, metallicity, star formation, and kinematics in a prototypical early disk galaxy.

shortlist.title: Quasar Impostors: Two Extremely UV-Bright ( M UV ≈ −23.5) Reionisation-Epoch Galaxies Powered by Very Massive Stars
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: The extreme bright end of the galaxy UV luminosity function during reionisation remains poorly constrained, particularly where the galaxy and quasar luminosity functions overlap and source classification becomes ambiguous. We present JWST/NIRSpec and ALMA Band-6 observations of J1450−0144 (z = 6.627) and J1429−0104 (z = 6.796), two MUV ≃ −23.5 sources originally classified as faint quasars by SHELLQs. NIRSpec reveals blue UV continua, strong P Cygni profiles in N v, Si iv, and C iv, broad He ii λ1640 emission with rest-frame equivalent widths of 8.8 ± 1.2 and 3.7 ± 1.1 Å, respectively, and narrow nebular lines, reclassifying both as extremely UV-luminous galaxies. Standard population-synthesis models cannot simultaneously reproduce the strong He ii and wind features, whereas models incorporating very massive stars (VMS; M ≳ 100 M⊙) with dedicated wind prescriptions can. These models favor a star-formation duration of 2–4 Myr for J1450−0144, with a broader allowed range for J1429−0104, stellar masses of log (M⋆/M⊙) ≈ 9.2–9.9, and star-formation rates of ≃ 300–540 M⊙ yr−1. Under the same VMS wind models, equivalent-width diagnostics imply Mup ≳ 225 M⊙ for J1429−0104, while J1450−0144 lies beyond even the Mup = 475 M⊙ grid. ALMA detects luminous [C ii] 158 μm emission in both systems, with L[CII] ≈ 0.8 and 4.1 × 109 L⊙, respectively. J1429−0104 additionally shows bright dust continuum, with both [C ii] and dust offset by ∼5.4 kpc from its UV emission. These sources demonstrate that VMS can power some of the most UV-luminous galaxies at cosmic dawn and show that source classifications, and hence the inferred demographics of both galaxies and quasars in the crossover regime, need revisiting.

Turbulent gas-rich discs at high redshift: the origin of early massive stellar bars
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Recent observations combining the power of ALMA and JWST inter alia have revealed large (3 − 7 kpc), massive (3 − 10 × 1010 M⊙) stellar bars at z = 4 − 5 when the Universe was only 1.2-1.6 Gyr old. At this early epoch, the host galaxy was baryon-dominated (typically 75% gas, 25% stars) within the observed extent of the disc (8 − 15 kpc). Using Nexus N-body/hydrodynamic simulations, we show that such bars can form promptly (400−800 Myr), provided the disc mass fraction is high (fdisc ≳ 70%) and the bar is gas-dominated at the time of its formation, consistent with the observations. In this limit, gas-free bars form more slowly (≈1 Gyr) and are weakened by vertical bending modes, but a substantial gas component suppresses this instability. Unlike massive bars in the local Universe, these early bars were sites of vigorous star formation, as we show. Remarkably, for gas-rich models with fgas ≲ 60%, the bars develop X-shaped boxy bulges; at higher gas fractions (fgas > 60%), diffusion suppresses resonant orbit trapping and the emerging bar collapses within 1 Gyr to form a classical bulge. The bar formation time, length, mass, and m = 2 Fourier amplitude are all inversely related to fgas. We present a simple analytic model for how stochastic forcing shifts the bar onset time, defined as the time at which the growing bar amplitude reaches a specified threshold.

shortlist.title: Collusion through Common Leadership
shortlist.abstract: This paper studies whether common leadership, defined as two firms sharing executives or board directors, contributes to collusion. Using an explicit measure of labor market collusion from unsealed court evidence, we find that the probability of collusion between two firms increases by 11 percentage points after the onset of common leadership, a ninefold increase over the baseline rate. These results are not driven by closeness of product or labor market competition. Our findings are consistent with the increasing attention toward common leadership under Clayton Act Section 8. shortlist.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τα∝B−2. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 1012 G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

shortlist.title: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial
shortlist.abstract: Incretin mimetics as obesity therapy induce substantial weight and fat loss but also decrease lean soft tissue mass, possibly impairing skeletal muscle function. Here, in this two-arm randomized controlled trial of adding resistance exercise (REx) to tirzepatide (T), 120 adults with overweight or obesity were treated with tirzepatide and randomized to thrice-weekly resistance exercise training or usual activities for 40 weeks. Tirzepatide was safe, and most participants tolerated up-titration to 15 mg weekly. Adherence to resistance exercise was 91%. Weight loss achieved was similar (T = -22.61 kg, T+REx = -22.28 kg, P = 0.694). For primary outcomes, loss of total fat mass was similar (T = -17.19 kg, T+REx = -17.98 kg, P = 0.700; between-group difference = -0.77 kg, 95% confidence interval (CI): -2.14 kg to 0.60 kg), but resistance exercise reduced loss of total lean soft tissue mass (T = -4.67 kg, T+REx = -3.57 kg, P < 0.001; between-group difference = 1.09 kg, 95% CI: 0.43-1.75 kg). For related endpoints, resistance exercise reduced loss of appendicular lean soft tissue mass (T = -3.55 kg, T+REx = -2.92 kg, P < 0.001). Upper and lower body muscle strength decreased with tirzepatide (bench press -4.09 kg, lat pulldown -4.42 kg, knee extension -4.42 kg) but increased with T+REx (+4.68 kg, +8.58 kg, +5.88 kg, respectively, all P < 0.001 versus tirzepatide). In conclusion, resistance exercise training attenuated loss of total lean soft tissue mass, representing an effective adjunct to tirzepatide anti-obesity therapy. shortlist.title: Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS Randomized Clinical Trial
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Information on the effects of tirzepatide, a once-weekly glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist approved for obesity management in adults with obesity, remains limited in adolescents. Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly tirzepatide in adolescents with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication. Design, Setting, and Participants: This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, 72-week clinical trial was conducted at 31 medical research centers and hospitals in Canada, the Czech Republic, Israel, Italy, Poland, and the US from October 16, 2023, to June 2, 2026, among adolescents aged 12 years to younger than 18 years with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication. Interventions: Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide, escalated to a maximum tolerated dose (5, 10, or 15 mg), or placebo for 72 weeks, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary end point was percent change in body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) from baseline to week 72. Key secondary end points included percentages of participants achieving BMI reductions of at least 5%, at least 10%, at least 15%, and at least 20%; changes in BMI SD score; BMI expressed as a percentage of the 95th percentile; and body weight, waist circumference, and physical functioning from baseline to week 72. Safety outcomes included treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events. shortlist.title: Enhancing Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning via Hierarchical Feature Optimization
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a compelling paradigm for privacy-preserving distributed machine learning, allowing multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model by transmitting locally computed gradients to a central server without exposing their private data. Nonetheless, recent studies find that the gradients exchanged in the FL system are also vulnerable to privacy leakage, e.g., an attacker can invert shared gradients to reconstruct sensitive data by leveraging pre-trained generative adversarial networks (GAN) as prior knowledge. However, existing attacks simply perform gradient inversion in the latent space of the GAN model, which limits their expression ability and generalizability. To tackle these challenges, we propose Gradient Inversion over Feature Domains (GIFD), which disassembles the GAN model and searches the hierarchical features of the intermediate layers. Instead of optimizing only over the initial latent code, we progressively change the optimized layer, from the initial latent space to intermediate layers closer to the output images. In addition, we design a regularizer to avoid unreal image generation by adding a small l₁ ball constraint to the searching range. We also extend GIFD to the out-of-distribution (OOD) setting, which weakens the assumption that the training sets of GANs and FL tasks obey the same data distribution. Furthermore, we consider the challenging OOD scenario of label inconsistency and propose a label mapping technique as an effective solution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve high-quality reconstruction and outperform competitive baselines across a variety of FL scenarios.

shortlist.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
shortlist.abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain’s proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is, for example, 1,2^(1/3),2^(-1/3) 1 , 2 1 / 3 , 2 − 1 / 3 . This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature (2,2) ( 2 , 2 ) . The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature (3,3) ( 3 , 3 ) in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on SL(2,Z)³ SL(2, R)³ SL ( 2 , Z ) 3 ∖ SL ( 2 , R ) 3 over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner’s measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

shortlist.title: Burst Spiking Neural Networks
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: A central goal of current Spiking Neural Network (SNN) research is to improve their accuracy toward becoming low-power alternatives to Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). This work further argues that realizing this ambition requires improving not only accuracy but also robustness, defined as the ability to maintain correct predictions under input perturbations. We identify two key issues in existing SNN methods that undermine robustness. First, binary spiking activations can produce large activation-state changes under small perturbations. Second, the lack of effective weight constraints makes network outputs more sensitive to input variations. To this end, we propose Burst Spiking Neural Networks (BuSNNs), built upon Burst-enhanced Spiking Neurons (BSNs) and a Dynamic Weight Constraint (DWC) mechanism. BSNs incorporate burst firing to provide a graded spiking pattern. This spiking mechanism mitigates perturbation-induced transitions in activation states and thereby enhances robustness. DWC penalizes connection weights based on activation states, effectively reducing weight magnitudes and improving robustness while preserving accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses to support these robustness effects. Experimental results further show that, on smaller-scale benchmarks such as CIFAR-10, BuSNNs outperform both SNN and ANN counterparts in accuracy and robustness. On large-scale ImageNet, BuSNN with the MS ResNet-34 backbone further improves top-1 accuracy and corruption robustness over the corresponding SNN baseline by 3.18% and 2.66%, respectively. Despite using spike-based activations, BuSNNs surpass 4-bit activation-quantized ANN baselines and approach 8-bit ANN baselines on ImageNet. They also preserve SNNs' low-power advantage with up to a 4.38× theoretical energy…

shortlist.title: A Plasma eMTBR-Tau Immunoassay for Detection of Advanced Insoluble Tau Pathology
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation. Objective: To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET). Design, Setting, and Participants: This cross-sectional study included brain donors with antemortem plasma from 2 US autopsy cohorts, and individuals with plasma samples and tau PET from 2 imaging cohorts in Canada and Sweden, with visits between 2002 and 2025 depending on the cohort. Exposures: Plasma eMTBR-tau measured with an immunoassay and eMTBR-tau243 measured with mass spectrometry. Main Outcomes and Measures: Plasma eMTBR-tau levels across neuropathologic Braak neurofibrillary tangle stages (I-VI, ranging from tangles confined to the entorhinal region to widespread neocortical tangles) and tau-PET Braak stages (0-VI), expressed as fold changes. Correlations with regional tau-PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs; higher values indicating more tau tangles), discrimination of regional tau-PET positivity (area under the curve [AUC]), and correlation with mass spectrometry-based eMTBR-tau243. Results: The study included 728 participants in 4 cohorts (median age by cohort, 71.0-83.5 years; 41.3%-56.6% female). In the 2 autopsy cohorts (n = 241 and n = 240), eMTBR-tau age- and sex-adjusted geometric means were 0.0021 pg/mL and 0.0040 pg/mL, respectively, at Braak stages I-II vs 0.107 pg/mL and 0.101 pg/mL at…

shortlist.title: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4+ T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity
shortlist.abstract: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4 + T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (T FH ) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 ( Tnfaip3 ) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating T FH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

shortlist.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear. Objective: To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies. Design, Setting, and Participants: This case-control study included 4 biorepositories based in the US that contributed CSF and plasma samples from participants with and without tauopathies, many of whom had antemortem biofluid samples paired with autopsy or genetically defined neuropathology. Samples were analyzed between August 2023 and December 2025. Data analysis occurred from August 2024 to July 2026. Exposure: CSF and plasma eMTBR-tau243 concentrations measured using a mass spectrometry-based assay. Main Outcomes and Measures: Outcomes included mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (eg, AD and CTE) based on autopsy, frontotemporal lobar degeneration with MAPT variants (FTLD-MAPT), and CTE stage. Differences in biomarker levels between groups were evaluated using analysis of variance or analysis of covariance, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the discriminative performance of fluid eMTBR-tau243. shortlist.title: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
shortlist.abstract: The economics of residential electrification in high-cost electricity regions remain uncertain. Using metered data from over 20,000 California homes, we assess the economic, environmental, and equity impacts of end-use electrification under rollout strategies based on household income and gas infrastructure age. Even under favorable electricity rates, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values (NPVs). Cost-effectiveness improves with deeper electrification scenarios, particularly when more costs are shifted to fixed charges and for homes with existing air conditioning—54–67% of these households break even when electrifying space heating, compared to fewer than 5% of those without. Income-based rebates more than double the share of low- and moderate-income households with positive NPVs. Prioritizing areas with aging gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions on par with high-income-led adoption and avoids costly pipeline replacement, but requires the highest subsidy to achieve cost-effectiveness across all households. These findings highlight trade-offs in designing equitable electrification strategies.

shortlist.title: HOPO 14-1, an Oral Actinide Chelator: A Phase 1 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Current treatments approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for internal actinide contamination (pentetate calcium trisodium and pentetate zinc trisodium) require intravenous injection or nebulized inhalation under medical supervision and have limited radionuclide coverage. HOPO 14-1, an oral form of 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO), is the first shelf-stable, broad-spectrum actinide chelator in clinical development that does not require intravenous access or trained personnel. In preclinical models, 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) removed a broad range of actinides, and its oral route supports scalable emergency medical use. Objective: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic parameters, and excretion of a single dose of HOPO 14-1 in healthy adults. Design, Setting, and Participants: This was a phase 1 nonrandomized clinical trial including 42 healthy adults (6 per dose level) with evaluations for 14 days after administration of a single dose and conducted at a single site in the US. Participants were recruited and screened between March 2023 and July 2025 and follow-up was completed in August 2025. Intervention: Single oral dose of HOPO 14-1 administered at 1 of 7 dose levels (100 mg, 200 mg, 500 mg, 1200 mg, 2500 mg, 5000 mg, or 7500 mg) with follow-up through day 14 after dose administration. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcomes were the incidence and severity of adverse events, drug-related adverse events, and serious adverse events. The secondary outcomes were plasma pharmacokinetic parameters and cumulative urinary and fecal excretion. Results: Of the 42 healthy adults enrolled (median age, 43 [IQR, 34-51] years; 64% female), all received a single dose of HOPO 14-1 (administered across all dose levels as assigned). shortlist.title: Long-term development of a motor memory
shortlist.abstract: Human behaviour is developed through continuous adaptation to our environment over a range of timescales. Extensive studies have investigated the mechanisms and computations underlying this process of sensorimotor adaptation using several hundred trials. However, most of our motor skills have had countless hours of practice. Here we study a simple motor adaptation task using thousands of training trials over multiple weeks to study the long-term development of a motor memory, and examine changes in adaptation, retention, interlimb transfer, decay, spontaneous recovery and generalization. Unlike previous studies, participants showed near complete compensation to the novel dynamics, along with long-term increases in retention and spontaneous recovery. Moreover, we find narrowing in the angular generalization, suggesting continual tuning of the motor memory to the task. This demonstrates the extensive changes occurring with longer training of motor tasks, highlighting their importance in studies of sensorimotor control, rehabilitation and training.

shortlist.title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
shortlist.abstract: Dementia incidence has been declining in Western societies for decades, but whether this reflects higher cognitive capacity entering old age, slower cognitive decline, or both remains unresolved. Analysing ~783,000 episodic memory assessments from ~219,000 individuals across five longitudinal cohorts, we find that later-born cohorts benefit from a double dividend: higher memory levels entering old age and slower rates of decline. The projected 20-year cohort advantage at age 80 is of sufficient magnitude to plausibly account for the observed 13% per-decade decline in dementia incidence reported in meta-analyses. Generational gains are disproportionately concentrated among the fastest-declining individuals, and are reflected in lower hippocampal atrophy rates in an independent sample. A formal bounding analysis shows that the double dividend is robust across a range of plausible period assumptions, consistent with environmental conditions operating across the lifespan having reshaped the architecture of human cognitive aging.

shortlist.title: How Sociotropic Aesthetic Judgments Drive Opposition to Dense Housing Development
shortlist.abstract: Voter opposition to dense housing development contributes to America’s housing shortage. Prevailing explanations emphasize homeowner self-interest and “NIMBYism.” We develop a theory of how sociotropic aesthetic judgments shape housing policy preferences and demonstrate its unique implications with a series of descriptive studies and experiments. First, people who choose to live in dense neighborhoods have an aesthetic taste for density, leading homeowners in already-dense areas to be more supportive of dense development both in their neighborhoods and elsewhere. Second, voters are more supportive of dense development when it is proposed in already-dense neighborhoods where it “fits”—even voters who live in those same dense neighborhoods. Finally, genuine aesthetic distaste for tall buildings is widespread and causally affects support for development. Our findings offer a new lens for understanding housing policy preferences and suggest novel solutions for addressing America’s housing shortage.

shortlist.title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
From Design to Disclosure
shortlist.abstract: We study the role of hard information in contractual and market settings in which the receiver can flexibly adjust allocations and transfers in response to the sender's disclosure. These settings include monopoly pricing, insurance contracting, and policy negotiations. Across these settings, the sender is worst off if she reveals her type completely because the receiver would then adjust the terms of trade to extract her surplus. Taking this feature as our central departure from the literature, we characterize the entire set of equilibrium payoffs in these disclosure games. We prove an equivalence result: a payoff profile can be approximated by an equilibrium of the disclosure game if and only if it can be achieved through information design. Thus, there exist equilibria in which the sender obtains approximately her commitment payoff.

shortlist.title: Do Fund Managers’ Commitments to Responsible Investing Affect Private Information Acquisition, Information Environment, and Corporate Sustainability?
shortlist.abstract: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. After committing to responsible investing (via United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI)), fund managers increase private information acquisition activities, that is, corporate site visits, particularly focusing on environmental and social issues. These visits generate negligible private investment value for the visiting funds. However, the information environment at the stock level improves following these visits with lower consensus analyst forecast errors. In addition to the information production role of these visits, they also generate positive externalities for other stakeholders through incremental improvements in the sustainability practices of the firms receiving sustainability-focused site visits from UNPRI fund managers. Collectively, the paper highlights the private costs and social benefits of responsible investing. This paper was accepted by Will Cong, finance. Funding: S. Agarwal and J. shortlist.title: Corporate Contributions to Ballot Measure Campaigns: Real Effects and Valuation
shortlist.abstract: We analyze novel data on corporate contributions to ballot initiatives at the U.S. state level. Firms make large contributions to ballot measure campaigns in favor of or against specific initiatives. They contribute significantly more to business initiatives compared with ideological initiatives. Corporate campaign spending is systematically associated with the likelihood that a ballot measure passes. Contributing firms experience changes in sales growth following the passage of important ballot measures. Following successful (failed) initiatives, all firms in affected industries exhibit significantly more positive (negative) cumulative abnormal returns around the election, but contributing firms do more so than peers. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Funding: R. Fahlenbrach gratefully acknowledges financial support from the Swiss Finance Institute. Conserved T cell receptor usage underpins recognition of CD1c presenting a mycobacterial lipid
shortlist.abstract: The mechanism by which αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) recognize mycobacterial lipids presented by CD1 family members is not well understood. We used CD1c tetramers loaded with the mycobacterial phosphomycoketide (PM) or mannosyl-PM to isolate T cells from healthy blood donors and individuals from a tuberculosis (TB)-endemic region of South Africa, with higher frequencies observed in individuals from the TB-endemic region. High-throughput analysis of >200 paired CD1c–mycoketide tetramer+ αβTCRs identified a conserved TCR motif, encoded by TRBV4-1 or TRBV7-9 variable region genes in greater than half of TCRs sequenced. A cryo-EM structure of a TRBV7-9+ TCR in complex with CD1c-PM demonstrated that the TCR bound to the A′-side of CD1c, directly contacting the phospholipid antigen and F′-portal residues. Analysis of multiple T cell clones interacting with CD1c mutants suggested that this TCR docking mode is representative of the larger TRBV7-9+ T cell population. Collectively, this study provides insight into mycobacterial lipid antigen recognition by αβ T cells restricted to CD1c.

shortlist.title: Aspiring to a Better Future: Can a Simple Psychological Intervention Reduce Poverty?
shortlist.abstract: Do higher aspirations for the future motivate people living in poverty to make long-term investments? Do their aspirations increase when economic conditions improve? To answer these questions, we run a 415-village field experiment with 8,300 women living in poverty in rural Kenya. We design an 80-minute workshop to help people set higher aspirations and plan to achieve them. We cross-randomise this with large unconditional cash transfers. The workshop substantially raises aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue, and living standards 17 months later, relative to a placebo workshop. Increases in aspirations are the most likely mechanism to explain the economic effects. Cash transfers also raise aspirations, which might help to explain why transfers increase labour supply and investment. We conclude that aspirations respond to both economic and psychological interventions, contribute to investment decisions and living standards, and are important considerations for development policy.

shortlist.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

shortlist.title: Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice
shortlist.abstract: Study Objectives Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a pervasive cardiovascular risk factor linked to accelerated aging. We investigated the underlying tissue-specific and systemic epigenetic mechanisms and the role of cellular senescence in the pathophysiology of OSA and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD). Methods C57BL/6J male mice were exposed to intermittent hypoxia (IH) or room air (RA) (n=25 mice/group) for 7 to 210 days. DNA methylation profiling was conducted on left cardiac ventricle and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the impact of IH duration was studied using regression models. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was calculated using a multi-tissue epigenetic clock. The role of p16-mediated senescence in IH-induced vascular dysfunction was assessed using transgenic mouse models (n=8 mice/group). Results IH exposures increased blood pressure and altered endothelial function in male mice. IH/RA differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were identified in left cardiac ventricle (n=5,747) and PBMCs (n=1,307), with minimal overlap (n=163, p=8.03 x 10-8). Both tissues differed in the EAA trajectory throughout the exposures. Epigenetic changes linked to cardiac dysfunction and cellular senescence, highlighting the Cdkn2a gene (encoding the p16 protein, a marker of cellular senescence). p16 expression was increased in aortic endothelial cells following IH. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve. Conclusions IH induces duration-dependent, tissue-specific epigenetic dysregulation and accelerated biological aging with p16-mediated cellular senescence as a primary driver. shortlist.title: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
shortlist.abstract: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. The combination of a sensor suite, estimators, and a low-level controller achieved centimeter-scale positional flight accuracy. In addition, we developed a hierarchical controller in which a human operator provides high-level commands to direct the robot's motion. In a 30-second flight experiment conducted outside a motion-capture system, the robot avoided obstacles and ultimately landed on a sunflower. This level of sensing and computational autonomy represents a notable advancement for the aerial microrobotics community, opening further opportunities to explore onboard planning and power autonomy.

fundamentals.title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
fundamentals.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft matter physics is to describe materials, such as the living cytoplasm and tissues, that are simultaneously active, chemically driven, and exhibit long-lasting memory of mechanical stresses. Here, we construct a generalized hydrodynamic framework at finite wave vectors and frequencies that is applicable to nonequilibrium fluids with memory. By leveraging stationary correlation identities, we derive a generalized linear response theory for nonequilibrium steady states. This framework serves as a formal extension of Onsager’s regression hypothesis beyond thermal equilibrium. Our approach provides a direct pathway to derive transport coefficients from steady-state fluctuations without the traditional Mori-Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, generalizing the Green-Kubo relations to nonequilibrium systems. As a corollary, we derive two model-free variants of the nonequilibrium fluctuation-response relation for non-Markovian dynamics. These generalized relations explicitly capture the nonequilibrium circulating currents—an out-of-equilibrium signature that is invisible to conventional scalar formulations or frameworks that treat degrees of freedom independently. Applying our theory to chemically driven active fluids reveals the emergence of active viscoelastic memory, wherein chemical reaction cycles dynamically renormalize the macroscopic viscous response. Strikingly, this active memory can induce negative storage modulus at finite frequencies, a behavior absent in ordinary viscoelastic fluids. Our first-principles framework rigorously extends linear rheology to nonequilibrium systems and provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian dynamics across a broad range of biological and synthetic active matter.

fundamentals.title: Origin of Electride States and Their Responses under Pressure
fundamentals.abstract: Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. While existing theoretical frameworks, including the interstitial quasi-atom (ISQ) and electron-ion interaction (EII) models, have provided some useful phenomenological interpretations of the electride formation, the atomistic origin and the underlying physics of this charge redistribution remain unclear. Here, within a first-principles framework, we systematically study the evolution of electronic structures of compressed materials, using alkali metals as representative examples. By mapping symmetry-resolved electronic band states onto atomic orbitals, we find that (i) pressure-induced quantum confinement raises the energies of atomic orbitals due to enhanced kinetic energy and increased overlap between valence and core electrons, with the energy shift being larger for more delocalized s orbital than for more localized p and d orbitals; and (ii) this effect causes reordering of band states, making the electride states, which are composed of the interatomic hybridized pd orbitals, to progressively shift in energy below the s orbital states, leading to their occupation and the onset of electride behavior. This microscopic electronic-state picture clarifies the origin of the electride formation and provides a general framework for understanding the evolution of interstitial electronic states under compression across diverse materials.

fundamentals.title: Spectral Small-Incremental Entangling: Breaking Quasipolynomial Complexity Barriers in Long-Range Interacting Systems
fundamentals.abstract: How the detailed entanglement structure emerges from quantum dynamics remains a fundamental challenge motivated by recent advances in quantum simulators and information processing. As a central milestone, the small-incremental-entangling (SIE) theorem bounds the entanglement-entropy growth rate but does not control the entanglement spectrum itself. In this work, we define the spectral-entangling strength, which quantifies how strongly an operator can reshape the distribution of Schmidt coefficients across a bipartition. We then prove a spectral-SIE theorem: for Rényi index α ≥ 1 / 2 , the growth rate of Rényi-entanglement entropies admits a universal bound. Remarkably, our bound at α = 1 / 2 is both qualitatively and quantitatively optimal; below this threshold ( α < 1 / 2 ), no universal speed limit on entanglement growth can exist. This result yields a sharp 1 / s 2 threshold in the tail of the ordered squared Schmidt coefficients, or equivalently in the entanglement-spectrum weights (with s the Schmidt index). It enables rigorous truncation-based-error control and establishes a quantitative link between entanglement-spectrum structure and computational complexity. As a practical highlight, for one-dimensional power-law interactions 1 / r η with η > 2 , this implies matrix-product-state approximations with bond dimension polynomial in ( n / ε ) for ground states, real-time evolved states, and Gibbs states, thereby closing the quasipolynomial gap, where n is the system size, and ε denotes the target approximation error in the relevant state or operator norm. By controlling Rényi entanglement, we further obtain a rigorous truncation-error bound for the time-dependent density-matrix renormalization-group scheme analyzed here. fundamentals.title: Dual Relaxation Modes Control Polymer Crystallization
fundamentals.abstract: Crystallization in polymers provides a fundamental probe of how molecular relaxation governs the emergence of order in glass-forming systems. Despite the longstanding success of the Lauritzen-Hoffman theory, its empirical treatment of molecular diffusion fails to capture the crystallization kinetics observed in the deeply supercooled regime. Here, we establish a physically grounded framework that replaces the empirical mobility in the Lauritzen-Hoffman formalism with a weighted combination of two measurable relaxation modes, namely the structural α relaxation, governing cooperative dynamics, and the slow Arrhenius process, associated with localized molecular rearrangements. This unified two-channel description quantitatively reproduces crystallization kinetics over several decades in time across 12 polymers spanning a wide range of fragility. In addition, our framework remains predictive under nanoconfinement, where interfaces and finite-size effects modify both mobility and nucleation. The results reveal that polymer crystallization proceeds through coupled long-range transport and localized ordering events governed by the same relaxation hierarchy that underlies vitrification, thus bridging glassy dynamics and crystallization kinetics at the molecular level.

fundamentals.title: Ordering of oxygen atoms in titanium revealed by superresolution electron ptychography
fundamentals.abstract: Interstitial atoms such as oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen are common point defects in crystalline solids and play important roles in determining electronic and mechanical properties. For decades, their behavior has been modeled assuming random spatial distributions owing to the lack of direct experimental access to their atomic-scale arrangements. Here, using oxygen-doped α-titanium as a model system, we overcome this fundamental limitation by achieving the first three-dimensional visualization, quantitative counting, and sub-[˚]Angstr¨om positioning of individual interstitial oxygen atoms in the bulk, enabled by super-resolution 4D-STEM ptychography with an adaptive prop agator. We find that interstitial oxygen atoms do not distribute randomly; instead, they exhibit correlated occupancy along the [0001] direction, giving rise to nanoscale ordered domains that are not detectable by conventional imaging. This discovery overturns the long-standing paradigm of randomness in interstitial systems and provides a microscopic foundation for understanding anomalous transport, strengthening, and phase stability in interstitial-engineered materials. Our approach establishes a general platform for atomic-scale defect metrology, opening avenues to ratio nally design materials through precise control of interstitial architectures in metals, semiconductors, and quantum solids.
fundamentals.topic: Advanced Electron Microscopy Techniques and Applications

fundamentals.title: First Principles Magnetohydrodynamical Theory for the Expanding Box Model: Effects on Expansion-induced Alfvén Wave Reflection
fundamentals.abstract: The expanding box model (EBM) has been widely employed to simulate multiscale plasma phenomena in the expanding solar wind by transforming the MHD equations to a comoving, noninertial frame. However, traditional formulations have suffered from historical ambiguity regarding the physical separation between the comoving and inertial reference frames, primarily arising from a classical approximation of an invariant magnetic field between them. To resolve this inconsistency, we reformulate the EBM from first principles using a fully covariant approach. Here, we model the expanding solar wind frame as an anisotropic expanding spacetime metric, allowing us to incorporate radial acceleration profiles and differential transverse expansion, ensuring that all physical fields are correctly transformed by expansion. We demonstrate that asymmetries identified in previous EBM-MHD literature are direct consequences of neglecting the tensorial scaling of the magnetic field. Our covariant treatment eliminates these residues, restoring symmetry in the comoving frame. Projecting our system back into the inertial frame clarifies the distinction between local plasma dynamics and plasma expansion, revealing the anisotropy of the Parker spiral as a geometric projection. Furthermore, linear wave analysis using Elsässer variables reveals that plasma expansion induces a low-frequency cutoff and geometric damping. Numerical integration demonstrates that expansion drives the reflection of Alfvén waves, generating counter-propagating modes primarily at low frequencies relative to the expansion rate, while high frequencies converge to the WKB approximation. This provides a consistent foundation for simulations, establishing that expansion can serve as a source of counter-propagating waves…
